children: State-owned energy giant Saudi Aramco reported a rise in third-quarter profit, offering some relief to the kingdom's finances during a period of escalating conflict with Yemen's Houthi militants.

The company's net profit rose 35% to $36.25 billion from $26.9 billion in the same period a year earlier, Aramco said Tuesday. It attributed the boost to higher crude volumes sold from maintaining consistent production, as well as higher prices of refined and chemical products.
Aramco declared a dividend of $21.9 billion, up 3.5% on year, which offers crucial support to Saudi Arabia's finances.
The results are a windfall at a challenging time for the Saudi Arabian government, as attacks from Iran-aligned Houthis intensify--resulting in damage to airports and other critical infrastructure.

Aramco said that as of Sept. 30, the impact of Houthi attacks on its facilities wasn't expected to be material to the company's financial position. Most of the more serious attacks occurred in October, after the third quarter ended.
